name: Syöjätär
body:
SYÖJÄTÄR
CR 10

This troll-like woman has scaly skin with an oily sheen associated with poisonous amphibians. Occasionally, one of the snakes growing from her scalp and hiding within her matted hair whips around.

XP 9,600
NE Large monstrous humanoid
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +20

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 10, flat-footed 23 (+1 Dex, +14 natural, ?1 size)
hp 123 (13d10+52)
Fort +10, Ref +9, Will +14
Immune disease, poison

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., burrow 20 ft.
Melee bite +18 (2d6+6 plus withering venom), 2 claws +18 (1d8+6 plus weakening venom)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks inflict muteness, weakening venom, withering venom
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 13th; concentration +17)

At will—contagion (DC 17), diminish plants
3/day—blight (DC 18), blindness/deafness (DC 16), spike stones (DC 18)
1/day—greater contagion (DC 19), insect plague, seeming (DC 19)

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 12, Con 18, Int 13, Wis 19, Cha 18
Base Atk +13; CMB +20; CMD 31
Feats Combat Casting, Deceitful, Great Fortitude, Intimidating Prowess, Iron Will, Pestilent, Skill Focus (Knowledge [nature])
Skills Bluff +21, Disguise +21, Intimidate +26, Knowledge (nature) +20, Perception +20
Languages Common
SQ corpse snakes

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Corpse Snakes (Su)

When a syöjätär dies, a venomous snake swarm erupts from her corpse.

Inflict Muteness (Sp)

A syöjätär can cast blindness/deafness to cause a target to become permanently unable to speak if its fails its save.

Weakening Venom (Ex)

Poison—Injury; save Fort DC 20; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d6 Str damage; cure 2 saves. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Withering Venom (Ex)

Poison—Injury; save Fort DC 20; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d4 Str damage; cure 2 saves. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any land
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Syöjätärs are the antithesis of nurturers, desiring nothing more than the destruction of life. They wander the earth withering plants and inflicting pestilence everywhere they roam. Their features change to match beasts regarded as unpleasant by the local inhabitants, as though they can scan the locals’ surface thoughts to learn what repels the locals. Likewise, when syöjätärs spread diseases, they inherently know which ones cause the most revulsion among those suffering from the maladies or witnessing the effects. One consistent feature is their wicked teeth and claws, tipped with venom that drains prey of vitality and might, respectively.

In rare instances, syöjätärs take a break from their devastation to indulge in their concept of whimsy, using their magic to take the appearance of influential people while disguising their targets as themselves and then blinding and muting their targets. These ruses put syöjätärs at the greatest personal risk, as others might discover their trickery and devise revenge plots against them. Destroying Syöjätärs does not immediately end the suffering and death they generate. Writhing masses of snakes erupt from their corpses almost immediately after they perish.
